The Contextual Help Asset Registry formalizes the problem of user comprehension under bounded rationality. We model the user as a sequential decision maker who observes a sequence of surfaces s_1, s_2, ... and must rapidly form a posterior belief about the utility u(s_i) of each. The goal is to minimize the expected time T until the user achieves a threshold level of confidence C_0 in their ability to act. The key challenge is that each help asset introduces a fixed cognitive cost c_a but reduces uncertainty by some amount \Delta H(u|v), where v is the visual/mediated signal. The optimal allocation strategy balances this tradeoff via a Lagrangian multiplier that equates marginal benefit to marginal cost. In the limit of many surfaces, this converges to a Poisson point process of registered assets, yielding a power-law distribution of surface-specific help density. Crucially, the registry must also account for heterogeneity in user prior knowledge, leading to a hierarchical Bayesian model where each user has a latent skill parameter \theta_i. The system then dynamically selects the help asset that maximizes expected mutual information gain I(T; V | S, \theta_i) across the population.
